- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Forecast tends to lag 1–2 days in upward moves — adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% for next day’s price.
- After sharp spikes (forecast > +3% from prior), reduce subsequent forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast deviates > 2% from 30-day moving average, revert toward average by 0.5–1% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.3) triggers downward correction — reduce forecast by 1–3% immediately.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment — dampen by 1–2% if sentiment is volatile or recent.
